passage: Monday: Uday held up Pallavi's pencil box in class. "This is so cheap. Mine cost way more." Some kids giggled. Pallavi's face burned, and she wanted the floor to swallow her. Tuesday: at lunch Uday started again about his new bag. Pallavi picked up her tiffin without a word and walked to the other bench, where Rekha and Ishan made room. Friday: on sports day, everyone's parents were on the sidelines except Uday's. He bragged louder than ever, listing things his family owned. Pallavi watched him, and something clicked: he looked like someone who needed to be noticed. She didn't answer him. She turned back to Rekha and Ishan and their game.

qa.q: What did Uday call Pallavi's pencil box?
How did Pallavi feel when Uday held up her pencil box, and what showed it?
qa.a: She felt ashamed; her face burned and she wanted the floor to swallow her.

qa.q: What choice helped Pallavi handle Uday's bragging, and why?
qa.a: Walking away to the bench with kinder friends worked, because she did not argue and stayed with people who made room for her.

qa.q: How might Uday be feeling on sports day when he brags louder than ever?
qa.a: Possibly insecure or lonely, since his parents were not on the sidelines and he seemed to want attention.

grounding: A child ashamed by a rich classmate's bragging sees that his words reflect his insecurity, not her worth, and stays with kinder friends.

passage:
In the Sehore government school, Vikas's father owned the rice mill, and Vikas never let anyone forget it. On Monday he picked up Madhav's dented tin geometry box and rattled it. "Cheap stuff. Mine's imported, see? Magnetic." A few boys laughed.
Madhav's face went hot. He grabbed the box back and stared at his desk. He wanted to shout that his father had bought it with a whole day's wages.
Instead he got up and went to the mango tree, where Salim and Kamla were sharing roasted chana. "Sit," Kamla said, and poured some into his palm.
Later, Madhav noticed something. Vikas bragged loudest on the days tests came back. Today he had got four out of twenty. Maybe the shiny box was all he had to feel good about.

qa.q: What did Vikas say about his own geometry box?
qa.a: That it was imported and magnetic.

qa.q: How did Madhav feel when the boys laughed?
qa.a: Ashamed and angry; his face went hot and he wanted to shout.

qa.q: What did Madhav choose instead of shouting, and why was it wise?
qa.a: He walked away to the mango tree and sat with kinder friends, which avoided a fight and kept him among people who valued him.

qa.q: What might be behind Vikas's bragging?
qa.a: Insecurity; he bragged loudest on test days and had scored four out of twenty, so the shiny box may have been his way to feel good.

grounding: A boy shamed by a richer classmate's bragging walks away to kinder friends and sees that the bragging shows the other boy's insecurity, not his own worth.

passage:
At the school gate in São Paulo, Rafael held up his new phone so everyone could see. Then he pointed at Yara's, with its cracked corner and stickers. "What is that, a brick? My grandmother has a better one."
A few kids snickered. Yara shoved her phone into her pocket, cheeks burning. Her brother had passed it down to her, and until that moment she had loved it.
She opened her mouth to say something mean about Rafael's ears. Then she closed it, turned around and walked to the bench where Beatriz was drawing. "Can I see?" Beatriz slid the sketchbook over.
From there Yara watched Rafael showing the phone to one group, then another, as if he needed every single person to be impressed. It didn't look like fun. It looked tiring.

qa.q: What did Rafael call Yara's phone?
What was Yara feeling when the kids snickered?
qa.a: Ashamed and embarrassed; her cheeks burned and she hid the phone she had loved.

qa.q: What did Yara do instead of insulting Rafael back?
qa.a: She walked away and sat with Beatriz, a kinder friend.

qa.q: What does Rafael's need to show the phone to group after group suggest?
qa.a: That he may need everyone's admiration to feel okay, which points to his insecurity rather than to Yara's worth.

grounding: A girl mocked by a wealthier classmate for her old phone feels ashamed, walks away to a kinder friend and sees the bragging as his insecurity.
